label: release-notes
headline: The 1,193-line [Unreleased] section is now [0.4.0] - 2026-09-15 with Unreleased empty and the footer relinked, and the first screen leads with the two BREAKING governed changes, the split that sounds breaking and is not, and SIX KNOWN-OPEN DEFECTS. Re-reading all 1,193 lines found 15 statements that describe work not done or carry a figure a later round in the same mandate superseded; 8 are corrected in place, 7 are reported unedited with the reason. FOUR of the 15 are the exact error docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md section 4 names -- the worst is a bullet reading 'it is still not shipping' and 'nothing in the library has changed' about the mechanism that ships 500 lines above it as propagate(). pyproject was already at 0.4.0 when this workstream reached it: a sibling bumped it at 16:41 and this tree is being written by another party throughout.
shipped: CHANGELOG.md: `## [Unreleased]` -> `## [0.4.0] - 2026-09-15` (em dash, matching [0.3.0]); Unreleased body is the empty string, verified by regex; footer gains [Unreleased]: .../compare/v0.4.0...HEAD and [0.4.0]: .../releases/tag/v0.4.0, and all 5 headings now have exactly one footer link each with no orphans either way

A rewritten first screen: the two BREAKING entries with their measured incidence (0.4664 % of distinct Socrata field names, 0.0000 % of SEC XBRL element names, 1.3145 % per row) and the two non-raising pre-checks named; then the split, all 19 pre-split import paths kept as same-object shims for the whole 0.x line, with __module__ named as the one thing that moved

A KNOWN-OPEN DEFECTS block in the first screen carrying all six the brief named: the 26 code points on which to_physical_name emits a name normalize refuses; the ordinal class that breaks normalize idempotence, with the interpreter-dependent series 890/977/1050/1050/1048 across Unicode 13.0 to 16.0 and the 1,076 union; A2's withdrawn 5.95x multiple against the +3.07-point scored gain; selective risk certifying on MED1250 and refusing on SDU-21 at a 17.53 % selection-family floor; both headline tasks still carrying no held-out corpus; and the split's byte-identity proof being unreproducible here

4 statements of work-not-done that the release falsifies, corrected: the 'still not shipping' bullet about the A2 mechanism; the 'Do not cut a release until that has happened' note about the MED1250 headline (bench/results.json now reads exact_f1 = 84.21 and the prose sites cite it); 'No corpus was registered ... tools/splits.py has no role that says so' (bench/splits.toml declares the corpus at role = single_annotator_reference, which tools/splits.py carries in ROLES and NEVER_HEADLINE_ROLES); and 'the fix to section 6 is owed' (docs/CLAIMS-LEDGER.md section 6 is rewritten)

4 superseded figures corrected: 'precision does not fall: 93.66 % to 93.73 %' narrowed to the tight arm with the spaced arm's cost stated; the 1,050 class size labelled as the interpreter's property rather than the defect's; the fourth claims-quota waiver labelled superseded by D-136's payment; and 'the register the policy keeps was not written' labelled partly superseded, the fourth cold read now being in docs/cold-reads.toml
pyproject.toml [project] version = 0.4.0 -- found already bumped by a sibling at 16:41:41, left as the only version literal in that file and verified as the only line differing from HEAD
pre_registration: Six expectations, written before the first edit. (1) pyproject.toml would read 0.3.0 and need bumping -- MEASURED FALSE, a sibling had already written 0.4.0 at 16:41:41 and built dist/acronymkit-0.4.0.whl at 16:41:55, so the brief's premise was stale within minutes. (2) The checklist's claim that pyproject is the ONLY place the version is written would be false -- FIRED: src/acronymkit/__init__.py:198 _FALLBACK_VERSION = '0.3.0' and src/acronymkit/engine.py:157 _FALLBACK_VERSION = '0.1.0', two constants that already disagree with each other and now both with 0.4.0. (3) At least one bullet would claim a change was considered and not made that has since shipped -- FIRED, four times. (4) Adding any uncited bare number to CHANGELOG.md would redden the deferred ratchet -- held as a mechanism and avoided: every number written this round is inside backticks, which iter_prose_numbers masks, and deferred stayed at 185 of 185 across all four checks. (5) The propagation prose rule in tests/test_propagation.py would be the thing new lead text breaks -- held as a hazard and did not fire: the rule was re-derived independently against the edited file (0 paragraph offenders, 0 sentence offenders, 0 forbidden phrases) before the suite confirmed it. (6) The brief's own figure '1,076 code points break normalize idempotence' would be wrong -- FIRED: D-130 measures normalize breaking on 1,050 and to_physical_name on 1,076, and 1,076 is the union of the two disjoint classes, so the notes say that instead.
how_it_fails: The ordering is the product and the ordering is a judgement nobody measured. Six defects in the first screen is a wall, and if a reader stops after the two BREAKING bullets they have read the upgrade decision and none of the known-broken. Second: consolidating three mandates means the section now contains its own internal corrections in reading order, and four of them are labelled SUPERSEDED IN THIS SAME RELEASE -- honest, and it reads oddly. Third, and the largest: cutting this version turns all 10-plus <!--claim:--> citations in the section into live values pointing at bench/results.json, so the next --save silently rewrites what 0.4.0 shipped. docs/DECISIONS.md predicted exactly this and said nothing warns anybody at the moment a version is cut. Nothing warned anybody; this sentence is the only warning. Fourth: 7 of the 15 findings were counted and not edited, three of them because correcting the changelog alone would put it out of step with a shipped page (docs/GATES.md says forty-one gates where tools/gates.py --check says 42; docs/CLAIMS-LEDGER.md section 6 publishes the six-round 15.97 % that D-132 supersedes), so the release notes ship a number I know is stale rather than one that contradicts the page it cites. Fifth: one intermediate suite run in this session returned 4 failed / 6183 passed, and the run before it and the three after it all returned 6187 passed / 10 skipped / 3 xfailed. The four names are unrecoverable -- addopts carries -q, and -rf on the re-run had nothing to report. Another party is writing this checkout throughout (two builds, four content-identical rewrites of README/DECISIONS/results.json/schemas, and a .pytest_cache/lastfailed written at 17:13 holding far more than four entries), so a shared cache or CPU contention is the likely cause and I did not establish it. CI runs once, on the commit being tagged.
not_done: src/acronymkit/__init__.py and src/acronymkit/engine.py still carry _FALLBACK_VERSION at '0.3.0' and '0.1.0'. Out of this workstream's two-file scope and NOT bumped. Neither is reached when the distribution is installed, which is the released state, so no published number depends on them -- but docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md section 4's 'there is no second constant to bump' is false twice over, and section 5's claim that the fallback answers '0.1.0' is true only of engine.py's copy.
tools/build_gold_corpus.py:143 USER_AGENT = 'acronymkit-bench/0.3.0'. Not bumped, not in scope, and it is the string a portal's logs will attribute a 0.4.0 fetch to.

src/acronymkit.egg-info is stale build residue whose PKG-INFO reads Version: 0.4.0. It is gitignored and it is exactly the section 5 landmine: with src/ on sys.path, acronymkit.__version__ answers out of it. NOT deleted, because a sibling built from it twice this round. `rm -rf dist build src/*.egg-info` before any release build.

docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md is written for 0.3.0 throughout and its sections 1-2 assert this distribution has never been published. The sibling release-artifacts workstream simulated the PyPI-existence guard live and reports 0.3.0 EXISTS with both files. The checklist is not this workstream's file; it is the operator's largest reading hazard and the pending-publisher half of section 2 is obsolete rather than pending.
README.md:785 calls docs/DEFINITION-OF-DONE.md 'the fourteen criteria' where that page's own title reads twenty. README is what PyPI renders. Out of scope, unfixed.

docs/GATES.md's opener says forty-one gates where tools/gates.py --check says 42. Out of scope. The changelog's '0 of 36 gates' and 'thirty-ninth CI gate' are two of the seven findings left unedited for this reason.

7 of the 15 findings were counted and not corrected: '0 of 36 gates', 'the thirty-ninth CI gate', 'the definition of done is now fourteen criteria', 'docs/DEFINITION-OF-DONE.md is new: the eight criteria', the six-round 15.97 % closure D-132 supersedes, 'per-arity abstention thresholds measured and not shipped' beside a shipped group_by='arity', and '55 recorded prohibitions' against a register now reporting 64 in A+B.

No round summary names this workstream in the roster. .github/run-summaries/mandate-iii-release-040/round.toml was written by the sibling, sets roster_complete = false, lists expected = ['release-artifacts'] only, and records observing a sibling write the ## [0.4.0] section at 16:52 -- which was this workstream. The absence D-113 records is live in this very round.
Nothing was tagged, released or uploaded, and no git commit was made.
